title: Walking, Gait and Balance Changes in Parkinson's
content: Parkinson's disease can affect walking, gait, posture and balance. A person may begin taking small or short steps, shuffle their feet, walk more slowly, drag the feet, reduce arm swing, have difficulty turning, or feel less steady while walking. Some people experience freezing of gait, where the feet temporarily feel stuck to the floor even though they are trying to move. Freezing may occur when starting to walk, turning, passing through narrow spaces or approaching obstacles. Balance and postural changes can increase the risk of falls. Small or shuffling steps and other gait changes can have many causes and do not by themselves confirm Parkinson's disease. Persistent or worsening walking or balance problems should be assessed by an appropriate healthcare professional.
